messages:
Maya: Quick design thread — proposal for a hierarchical KV cache keying + persistence + invalidation scheme to make autotuner/kernel-path rollouts safer and cheaper. TL;DR: versioned prefixes + kernel-profile tags + seqlen buckets + lazy invalidation. PTAL.

Chris R.: Can you sketch the concrete key format? also how do we handle driver restarts and model rollouts without nuking the whole cache? :eyes:

Maya: Sketch below (Redis-style keys for clarity):
```
cache:{model_epoch:v12}:{model_hash:ab12cd}:{kernel:cudaA100_fp16_autotune_v3}:{seq_bucket:<=128}:{prefix_sha256:fe34...}
meta:{model_epoch:v12}:{model_hash:ab12cd} -> {"kernels":["cudaA100_fp16_autotune_v3","cudaA100_int8_v1"], "created_at":1680000000}
```
- model_epoch is bumped on config/driver changes (fast invalidation marker)
- keep model_hash for full-compat checks (rare)
- seq_bucket is coarse (<=32, 33-128, 129-512, >512) to avoid explosion of keys
- store small metadata blob per (epoch, model) so we can GC kernel-specific keys safely

Jun: A few operational notes:
- Persist cache to RocksDB on disk for Private installs; Redis for Hosted (with RDB/AOF). Keep metadata replicated separately so we don't rely on scanning keys for GC.
- Invalidation: never do eager global deletes in prod. Instead: increment model_epoch -> readers treat mismatched epoch as stale and skip. Stale entries get lazily reclaimed by background janitor.
- Add per-kernel TTLs: newer autotuner picks get longer TTLs, experimental kernels get short TTLs (e.g. 1h).

Leo: Two concerns: kernel selection can change per-request (autotuner experimenting). If kernel tag changes, keys won't match and we get misses -> regen -> possible thundering herd. Ideas:
- On miss, allow fallback to a compatible kernel key map: try `kernel:compat:{kernel_family}` before full recompute.
- Negative cache warms: small short-lived negative entries for prefixes that were just evicted to reduce regen churn.
- Background rehashing: reactor job that migrates hot prefixes to the new kernel tag with rate limits.

Chris R.: We've seen regressions with similar changes before. Attached quick profiling:
```
Before rollout: cache_hit_rate=0.92, p95_latency_ms=18, tokens/sec=120k
After rollout: cache_hit_rate=0.60, p95_latency_ms=38, tokens/sec=72k
```
Root cause analysis: sudden mismatch in `kernel` tag due to autotuner switching to `autotune_v3` but persisted entries used `autotune_v2`. The eager delete we ran then bumped disk IO and caused tail spikes.

SRE Ops: +1 on model_epoch marker. Operational tweaks to propose:
- Add warm-up rate limit: max N regenerations/sec per model_epoch to avoid storm.
- Instrumentation: emit `cache_entry_epoch`, `kernel_tag`, `seq_bucket`, and `regen_source` (compute|fallback|migrate) as dimensions.
- Alert rule: drop in cache_hit_rate > 15% for 5m -> paging.

Maya: Implementation plan I'm proposing:
1) Prototype hierarchical keying in runtime branch (small PR) with `model_epoch` support and seq_bucketing.
2) Add metadata store (RocksDB/Redis hash) for epochs + kernel families.
3) Implement lazy invalidation: epoch bump causes reads to ignore old entries; janitor migrates hot entries over time.
4) Add short negative cache entries and a regen rate limiter.
5) Canary rollout to 10% traffic, measure hit_rate and p95.

Jun: For persistence: ensure we snapshot metadata frequently and run verification at cold-start: compare model_epoch in metadata with driver config and evict orphaned kernel entries (fast path).

Leo: Minor: for seq_bucket boundaries use measured distribution from profiling instead of fixed buckets. Also add a telemetry counter for "fallback kernel attempts" so autotuner can learn penalty.

Chris R.: I'll take the canary metrics dashboard and the alert thresholds. Will also add an automated perf-check that fails CI if p95 increases >10% on synthetic load.

SRE Ops: Can we also include a small playbook for rollback? i.e., how to force global epoch increment so old entries become inert without deleting them? That should be a single control-plane flip.

Maya: Yes — control-plane action is `bump_model_epoch(model_id)` which writes new epoch and signals runtime. We'll expose a one-click in Console for emergencies.

dev-bot: deploy-bot posted: "canary/runtime-cache-keying v1.3 deployed to 10%" :rocket:

Maya: Action items: @Chris R. dashboard + alerts; @Jun persistence API + janitor design; @Leo regen rate limiter + fallback map; SRE Ops to draft playbook. I'll open the runtime PR with sketches tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:
